analyst_view.overall: Early view: PSG top the table with four wins from four and 20 goals, including 6-0 at Villarreal on matchday 4. Aston Villa are sixth on nine points but were beaten 3-0 at Barcelona and then drew 4-4 at Manchester United on Sunday, conceding twice inside the first four minutes. Villa were without Onana, Ruggeri and Wan-Bissaka at Barcelona; PSG had Kvaratskhelia (cruciate ligament), Dembélé and Marquinhos (hamstrings) out earlier in the phase.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 1.8 of them Villa's. I lean higher, mainly on PSG's side: they have scored 20 in four league-phase games and broke a scoring record, while Villa conceded three at Barcelona and four at Old Trafford in their last two games. Villa have scored 12 in Europe, so they should still get chances at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, split almost evenly. I would leave it: PSG should have more of the ball, but Villa will still attack at home, as they showed by scoring four at Old Trafford through Alysson, Jackson, McGinn and Goretzka.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. I see no reason to move it: Villa had only two bookings in the chaotic 4-4 at Old Trafford, and PSG's possession game rarely forces opponents into lots of fouls. A Villa side fighting to stay in the top eight could get a little edgier late on.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.3 shots, with PSG on 16. I lean slightly higher: PSG average well over four goals a game in this phase, which only comes with heavy shot volume, and Villa at Villa Park will take their chances rather than sit in a low block.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target. That fits a game with two attacking sides and two shaky defences, so I keep it. Fabián Ruiz, João Neves and Doué all scored at Villarreal, so the threat is spread across PSG's side.
